title: Pregnancy and Development

# Pregnancy and Development

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the development of the embryo and fetus
- Explain the functions of the placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic fluid
- Describe the role of hormones during pregnancy
- Understand factors affecting fetal development

## Introduction

**Pregnancy** (gestation) is the period from implantation to birth, lasting approximately 40 weeks in humans. During this time, a single cell develops into a fully formed baby, supported by specialised structures like the placenta and amniotic sac.

## Key Concepts

### Stages of Development

| Period | Time | What's happening |
|--------|------|------------------|
| Pre-embryonic | Week 1-2 | Cleavage, implantation |
| Embryonic | Week 3-8 | Organs form |
| Fetal | Week 9-40 | Growth and maturation |

### Embryonic Development (Weeks 3-8)

**Critical period:**
- All major organs begin to form
- Most vulnerable to damage
- Called organogenesis

**Key events:**
| Week | Development |
|------|-------------|
| 3 | Neural tube forms, heart begins |
| 4 | Heart beats, limb buds appear |
| 5 | Eyes, ears developing |
| 6 | Fingers, toes forming |
| 7 | All organs present |
| 8 | Recognisably human |

[DIAGRAM: Embryo development stages]

### Fetal Development (Weeks 9-40)

**Focus:** Growth and maturation of organs

| Trimester | Weeks | Key developments |
|-----------|-------|------------------|
| First | 1-12 | Organs form; heartbeat detectable |
| Second | 13-26 | Movement felt; sex visible; viable ~24 weeks |
| Third | 27-40 | Rapid growth; lungs mature; head down |

**Size progression:**
| Week | Length (crown-rump) | Weight |
|------|---------------------|--------|
| 12 | 6 cm | 18 g |
| 20 | 16 cm | 300 g |
| 28 | 25 cm | 1 kg |
| 40 | 36 cm | 3-4 kg |

### The Placenta

**Structure:**
- Develops from trophoblast (blastocyst outer layer)
- Disc-shaped organ
- Connected to baby by umbilical cord
- Maternal and fetal blood come close but don't mix

[DIAGRAM: Placenta structure showing villi]

**Functions:**

| Function | How |
|----------|-----|
| Gas exchange | O₂ from mother → fetus; CO₂ from fetus → mother |
| Nutrition | Glucose, amino acids, vitamins diffuse to fetus |
| Waste removal | Urea from fetus → mother's blood |
| Protection | Barrier to some pathogens |
| Hormone production | Produces progesterone after week 10 |

### Placental Exchange

**What crosses the placenta:**

| Beneficial | Harmful |
|------------|----------|
| Oxygen | Alcohol |
| Glucose | Nicotine |
| Amino acids | Some drugs |
| Vitamins | Some viruses (rubella) |
| Antibodies | Some bacteria |
| Water | Carbon monoxide |

**Blood doesn't mix because:**
- Different blood types possible
- Mother's pressure too high for fetal vessels
- Thin barrier allows diffusion

### The Umbilical Cord

**Structure:**
- Connects fetus to placenta
- ~50 cm long at birth
- Contains two arteries, one vein

**Blood vessels:**
| Vessel | Carries | From → To |
|--------|---------|----------|
| Umbilical arteries (×2) | Deoxygenated blood | Fetus → placenta |
| Umbilical vein (×1) | Oxygenated blood | Placenta → fetus |

**Note:** Opposite to normal - artery carries deoxygenated blood!

### Amniotic Fluid and Sac

**Amniotic sac:** Membrane surrounding fetus

**Amniotic fluid:**
| Function | How it helps |
|----------|-------------|
| Protection | Cushions against bumps |
| Temperature | Maintains constant temperature |
| Movement | Allows fetus to move and develop muscles |
| Prevents adhesion | Stops membranes sticking to fetus |
| Sterile environment | Protects from infection |

### Hormones During Pregnancy

| Hormone | Source | Function |
|---------|--------|----------|
| hCG | Placenta | Maintains corpus luteum early on |
| Progesterone | Corpus luteum → placenta | Maintains endometrium; prevents contractions |
| Oestrogen | Ovaries → placenta | Develops breast tissue; prepares for labour |
| Relaxin | Ovaries | Relaxes ligaments for birth |

**Timeline:**
- Weeks 1-10: Corpus luteum produces progesterone
- After week 10: Placenta takes over

### Factors Affecting Development

**Harmful factors:**

| Factor | Risk |
|--------|------|
| Smoking | Low birth weight, premature birth, SIDS |
| Alcohol | Fetal alcohol syndrome |
| Drugs | Birth defects, addiction |
| Poor nutrition | Developmental problems |
| Infections (rubella) | Birth defects |
| Radiation | Mutations, birth defects |

**Beneficial factors:**
- Balanced diet
- Folic acid supplements
- Regular prenatal care
- Avoiding harmful substances

### Folic Acid

**Why important:**
- Prevents neural tube defects
- Should be taken before conception
- Critical in first 12 weeks

### Multiple Pregnancies

| Type | How formed | Genetics |
|------|------------|----------|
| Identical twins | One egg splits | Identical DNA |
| Fraternal twins | Two eggs fertilised | Different DNA |

## Common Exam Questions

- Describe the functions of the placenta
- Explain how the fetus obtains oxygen and nutrients
- Describe the role of amniotic fluid
- Explain why smoking during pregnancy is harmful

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** Maternal and fetal blood mix in the placenta
- **Reality:** They come close but remain separate

- **Misconception:** The umbilical vein carries deoxygenated blood
- **Reality:** It carries oxygenated blood from placenta to fetus

- **Misconception:** The placenta filters out all harmful substances
- **Reality:** Many harmful substances can cross

- **Misconception:** The fetus breathes air in the womb
- **Reality:** Oxygen comes from mother's blood via placenta

## Practice Questions

1. Name two functions of the placenta. (2 marks)

2. Explain how oxygen passes from mother to fetus. (2 marks)

3. Describe the functions of the amniotic fluid. (3 marks)

4. Explain why maternal and fetal blood do not mix. (2 marks)

5. Explain why smoking during pregnancy can harm the developing fetus. (3 marks)

6. Describe how the fetus obtains nutrients and removes waste products during pregnancy. Include the role of the placenta and umbilical cord. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Embryo | Developing human from week 3-8 |
| Fetus | Developing human from week 9-birth |
| Placenta | Organ for exchange between mother and fetus |
| Umbilical cord | Connects fetus to placenta |
| Amniotic fluid | Fluid surrounding fetus |
| Gestation | Period of pregnancy |
| Trimester | One-third of pregnancy (~13 weeks) |
| hCG | Hormone produced by placenta |

## Summary

- Embryonic period (weeks 3-8): organs form
- Fetal period (weeks 9-40): growth and maturation
- Placenta: gas exchange, nutrition, waste removal, protection
- Maternal and fetal blood don't mix; exchange by diffusion
- Umbilical cord: two arteries (deoxygenated), one vein (oxygenated)
- Amniotic fluid: cushioning, temperature, movement, protection
- Harmful substances (alcohol, nicotine, drugs) can cross placenta
- Folic acid prevents neural tube defects
